errors.english: Therefore, how could the awareness of the past and so forth be a direct perception ...
errors.why: The sentence continues on the next side (ཡིན་ཏེ། ... བསྐྱེད་པ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ) as an explanation of HOW cognition of the past is perception, not a rhetorical denial that it is.

note: A faithful rendering of a dense pratyakṣa argument; only the closing clause leans toward a rhetorical denial the commentary does not intend.

errors.english: the nectar-like essence of the Vinaya's Dharma and Sugata
errors.why: The phrase is 'the nectar-essence of the Sugata's Dharma-Vinaya'; the genitive is misparsed.

fix.find: the nectar-like essence of the Vinaya's Dharma and Sugata
fix.replace: the nectar-like essence of the Sugata's Dharma and Vinaya

note: Sound rendering of Guṇaprabha-related Vinaya commentary on quorum and purification by confession or resolve; one misparsed genitive.

errors.english: You have heard words from the Noble Udāyin that we never even heard
errors.why: The women complain that WE (བདག་ཅག) have heard from Udāyin words never heard before even from drunkards, gamblers and bastards.

fix.find: You have heard words from the Noble Udāyin that we never even heard
fix.replace: We have heard words from the Noble Udāyin that we never before heard

errors.english: speaks corrupt, sinful words about sexual intercourse to women
errors.why: The rule qualifies the words as 'not fit to be uttered in company' (ཚོགས་པར་མི་དབྱུང་བ), dropped here and in the narrative.

note: Good rendering of the saṅghāvaśeṣa on lewd speech; the women's complaint has the wrong pronoun.

errors.english: and its cause does not turn into darkness
errors.why: The lamp does not itself become red (དམར་པོ), a pun on rakta 'red/attached' that the next line resolves with ཆགས་པ; 'darkness' loses the point of the simile.

note: A readable and largely faithful verse rendering of the Buddha's declaration on the road to Vārāṇasī; the lamp simile's red/attachment pun is lost.

errors.english: when inferring the concomitant factor of the form of taste, it is like the relationship between form and taste themselves
errors.why: The example is: when one infers [the cause of] taste as a co-operating cause of form, as with form and taste; 'the form of taste' misparses the genitives.

errors.english: inferring that rain has fallen based on the movement of ants carrying their eggs
errors.why: The standard example (and the next line, འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཆར་པ) is inferring rain that is about to fall from the ants' movement, not rain that has already fallen.

note: The argument about inferring from taste to form is mostly followed, but the example sentences are muddled in places.

errors.why: This completes the opponent's proposal from the previous side (འོ་ན་ད་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ནི...): 'Then nirvāṇa is a non-entity', which the following verse refutes.

errors.english: one line of text not fully transcribed
errors.why: Nothing is missing; the sentence simply continues on the next side ('...both an entity and a non-entity'), and the unmarked remark is not translation.

note: A faithful rendering of the MMK 25 verses and commentary, except that the opening sentence inverts the opponent's thesis.
A faithful rendering of Avalokitavrata's account of the Sautrāntika position and of the 'as before' refutation.

errors.english: when the presence and absence of that contradictory reason are ascertainable, it serves as the proponent's proof, or becomes a refutation by the respondent
errors.why: Two items are paired here: the [valid] reason and the contradictory reason, which become the proponent's proof and the respondent's refutation respectively; the English collapses them into one.

note: A careful rendering of a difficult passage on the indeterminate reason; one pairing is collapsed.
A faithful rendering of the Kāśyapaparivarta passage on falsely claiming attainment and accepting offerings.

errors.english: where could there ever be the mistaken conception that something both exists and is permanent?
errors.why: འཁྲུལ་པ here is the logical deviation (vyabhicāra) of the reason 'existence' (an existent that is permanent would make it deviate), not a 'mistaken conception'.

note: A sound rendering of the momentariness argument (vināśitvānumāna) with good technical vocabulary; one term is taken in its everyday sense.
